# Ospex

> Ospex is a zero-vig peer-to-peer sports prediction protocol on Polygon. It provides neutral settlement infrastructure where agents — market makers, sharps, recreational bettors — operate on top. The protocol does not charge vig; agents set their own pricing. Ospex supports moneyline, spread, and total markets for NBA, NHL, NCAAB, MLB, NFL, and NCAAF.

## Thesis

Ospex is settlement infrastructure for sports prediction markets, not a sportsbook. A maker signs an EIP-712 off-chain commitment that names a side, a stake size, and the odds. A taker matches that commitment on-chain through MatchingModule, which opens a position on each side in PositionModule. Odds are uint16 integer ticks with ODDS_SCALE = 100, so 1.91x is the tick 191 and 2.50x is 250.

When the underlying game finishes, an off-chain Chainlink CRE (Chainlink Runtime Environment) workflow verifies the contest and reports the final score on-chain through the CreOracleReceiver; settlement is permissionless, and winners then claim their positions. Zero vig — no house edge, and all value flows between participants. The frontend is intentionally minimal: Ospex is built for programmatic agents first, through the SDK and CLI.

## Technical Details

- Chain: Polygon mainnet (chain ID 137)
- Token: USDC (6 decimals) at `0x3c499c542cEF5E3811e1192ce70d8cC03d5c3359`
- Oracle: Chainlink CRE — an off-chain workflow verifies and scores contests against three independent sports-data sources and reports on-chain to `CreOracleReceiver`. There is no Chainlink Functions router, no DON subscription, and no per-call LINK; CRE execution is funded off-chain by the workflow owner. Oracle requests (verify / market update / score) are permissionless, and an unscored contest auto-voids and refunds principal after a cooldown.
- Oracle governance: the CRE workflow is owned by `OspexCreTimelock`, a per-action timelock on Ethereum mainnet — a 7-day delay applies to workflow code/lifecycle changes (observable on-chain before they take effect). It cannot move or trap protocol funds: settlement is immutable and PositionModule has zero admin functions.
- Odds: uint16 integer ticks, ODDS_SCALE = 100 — e.g. 191 = 1.91x, 250 = 2.50x; valid range 101 to 10100
- Deployed 2026-06-28 (Round 5, the CRE oracle migration; Polygon block 89322650); all contracts verified on Polygonscan. The protocol is finalized and zero-admin — after `finalize()` no address holds any privileged on-chain capability.

### Governance (Ethereum Mainnet)

- OspexCreTimelock (CRE workflow owner / oracle governance): `0x40047BAFcdEd16C938058b7b67186299a2893561` on Ethereum mainnet (chain ID 1). This is a distinct contract from the Polygon OspexCore that happens to share the same address — both were the first contract (nonce 0) deployed by the same one-time deployer, and CREATE addresses depend only on (deployer, nonce), not the chain.

## SDK + CLI

`@ospex/sdk` and `@ospex/cli` (the `ospex` binary) are the recommended way for agents (and humans) to interact with the protocol — read protocol state, submit EIP-712 commitments, settle/claim positions, and subscribe to streaming odds. Distribution is via GitHub Releases tarballs (not npm): the `ospex` CLI ships as a single self-contained bundle — install it globally (`npm install -g` / `yarn global add` the `ospex-cli` release tarball) and run bare `ospex`; the separate `@ospex/sdk` tarball is the unbundled library for programmatic consumers. See https://ospex.org/downloads for the latest version, or https://github.com/ospex-org/ospex-sdk/blob/main/docs/QUICKSTART.md for the full walkthrough.
